answers.answer: Arrow diagram: arrows from 1 to 3, 4, 5 and from 2 to 3, 4, 5, for X×Y = {(1, 3), (1, 4), (1, 5), (2, 3), (2, 4), (2, 5)}.
solution: Draw two ovals. Write the elements of X (1 and 2) in the left oval.
Write the elements of Y (3, 4 and 5) in the right oval.
Each ordered pair is an arrow from its first projection (in X) to its second projection (in Y).
Draw arrows from 1 to 3, from 1 to 4 and from 1 to 5.
Draw arrows from 2 to 3, from 2 to 4 and from 2 to 5.
This gives 6 arrows, one for each of the 6 ordered pairs of X×Y.

answers.answer: Cartesian diagram: plot the 6 points (1, 3), (1, 4), (1, 5), (2, 3), (2, 4), (2, 5) on a perpendicular net, with X horizontal and Y vertical.
solution: Draw a horizontal line and a vertical line meeting at O.
Mark the elements of X (1, 2) on the horizontal line.
Mark the elements of Y (3, 4, 5) on the vertical line.
Draw a vertical line through each of 1 and 2.
Draw a horizontal line through each of 3, 4 and 5.
Mark the 6 points where these lines meet: (1, 3), (1, 4), (1, 5), (2, 3), (2, 4), (2, 5).
These 6 points are the cartesian diagram of X×Y.

answers.answer: Cartesian diagram: a perpendicular grid with X = {1, 2} on the horizontal axis and Y = {3, 4, 5} on the vertical axis; six points marked at (1, 3), (1, 4), (1, 5), (2, 3), (2, 4), (2, 5).
